usage: truesense [-h] [--json] [-V] area ...

truesense: command line for the Acer Predator Helios 16 (PH16-71).   truesense <area> <verb> ...   (every setting has on / off / toggle / status; --json for scripts)

positional arguments:
  area
    status       everything at a glance
    sensors      temperatures and fan RPM
    power        power mode (quiet balanced performance turbo eco) and the
                 automatic profile
    mode         a look and a fan curve for each power mode, applied when the
                 mode changes
    fan          fans: firmware auto, max, manual %, smart curve
    battery      80 % charge limit, charge to full once, calibration, USB
                 power-off charging
    display      LCD overdrive
    boot         boot animation and sound
    gpu          GPU mode (MUX); a change needs a reboot
    rear         rear light bar
    update       check for a newer TrueSense and install it
    look         saved lighting looks (keyboard effect/brightness/colours +
                 rear light)
    startup      what the lights and profile do at login
    keyboard     keyboard lighting
    audio        output, microphone, headset jack, Purified Voice, DTS
    keys         PREDATOR key and Fn+Esc: what each gesture does
    profile      named bundles of settings (gaming, quiet, battery-saver,
                 yours)
    cpu          CPU power limits and the guarded undervolt
    touchpad     touchpad on/off (Fn+F10)
    service      the daemon
    config       configuration
    doctor       check the whole stack and say how to fix problems
    selftest     set -> read back -> restore every firmware feature
    completion   shell completion script
    gui          the small optional window
    probe        read-only report of this laptop for model support (never
                 writes a setting)
    tui          the full control surface in the terminal (keyboard and mouse)
    daemon       run the daemon (systemd does this)

options:
  -h, --help     show this help message and exit
  --json         machine-readable output
  -V, --version  show program's version number and exit

Examples:
  truesense status
  truesense power set turbo
  truesense fan set 60
  truesense rear set breathing --color 00ff88
  truesense keyboard effect wave --brightness 50
  truesense keys set double output-toggle
  truesense profile apply gaming
  truesense doctor

AREA status
usage: truesense status [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

======================================================================
AREA power
usage: truesense power [-h]
                       {status,list,set,next,prev,smart,auto,hold,release,managers,game} ...

positional arguments:
  {status,list,set,next,prev,smart,auto,hold,release,managers,game}
    smart               Smart auto profiles: list | current | show NAME | use
                        NAME | copy NAME [NEW] | save NAME [--from BASE] --set
                        key=value ... | delete NAME (built-in profiles are
                        read-only: copy them to edit)
    auto                automatic power mode: off | native (PredatorSense-
                        like: power source only) | smart (heat, load and
                        battery aware); on = smart
    hold                keep the current power mode against the automatic
                        profile
    release             end a hold
    managers            other power managers (auto-cpufreq, TLP, tuned, power-
                        profiles-daemon, system76-power): list | stop
                        (TrueSense manages power: stops them, sets sane CPU
                        defaults, remembers) | restore
    game                game rules: a program raises the power mode while it
                        runs: list | add NAME MODE | remove NAME | clear

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

======================================================================
AREA mode
usage: truesense mode [-h] {bindings,bind,unbind,apply} ...

positional arguments:
  {bindings,bind,unbind,apply}
    bindings            what each power mode is bound to
    bind                bind a power mode to a saved look and/or a fan curve
                        (the service keeps a copy and applies it when the mode
                        changes; a curve only while the fans are on Smart)
    unbind              remove a mode's binding (nothing is changed on the
                        machine)
    apply               apply a mode's binding now (default: the current mode)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

--------------------------------------------------
VERB mode bindings
usage: truesense mode bindings [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

--------------------------------------------------
VERB mode bind
usage: truesense mode bind [-h] [--look LOOK] [--curve CURVE]
                           {quiet,balanced,performance,turbo,eco}

positional arguments:
  {quiet,balanced,performance,turbo,eco}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --look LOOK           a saved or built-in look
  --curve CURVE         a saved or built-in fan curve (not native)

--------------------------------------------------
VERB mode unbind
usage: truesense mode unbind [-h] [--look] [--curve]
                             {quiet,balanced,performance,turbo,eco}

positional arguments:
  {quiet,balanced,performance,turbo,eco}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --look                remove only the look
  --curve               remove only the fan curve

======================================================================
AREA fan
usage: truesense fan [-h] {status,auto,max,off,set,curve,smart} ...

positional arguments:
  {status,auto,max,off,set,curve,smart}
    auto                firmware control (0 rpm when cool)
    off                 stop both fans (needs --confirm; only when cool; the
                        service returns them to Auto if it gets warm)
    set                 manual duty per fan, 20..100 %, or 0 to stop that fan
                        (needs --confirm, only when cool)
    curve               smart-fan curves: list | current | show NAME | use
                        NAME | copy NAME [NEW] | save NAME --cpu PTS --gpu PTS
                        | delete NAME (built-in curves are read-only: copy
                        them to edit)
    smart               the daemon's smart curve

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

--------------------------------------------------

usage: truesense fan status [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

options:

VERB fan off

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --confirm   I understand the laptop can overheat with the fans off

VERB fan set
usage: truesense fan set [-h] [--confirm] cpu [gpu]

positional arguments:
  cpu
  gpu

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --confirm   I understand a stopped fan can let the laptop overheat

--------------------------------------------------
VERB fan curve
usage: truesense fan curve [-h] [--cpu CPU] [--gpu GPU]
                           [--hysteresis HYSTERESIS] [--down-rate DOWN_RATE]
                           [--predict PREDICT] [--couple COUPLE]
                           [--battery-shift BATTERY_SHIFT] [--from BASE]
                           [{list,current,show,use,save,delete,copy}] [name]
                           [new]

positional arguments:
  {list,current,show,use,save,delete,copy}
  name
  new                   copy: the new name

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --cpu CPU             CPU points, e.g. 52:0,60:35,70:55,80:75,89:100
                        (temperature:percent, 0 = firmware auto)
  --gpu GPU             GPU points
  --hysteresis HYSTERESIS
  --down-rate DOWN_RATE
  --predict PREDICT
  --couple COUPLE
  --battery-shift BATTERY_SHIFT
  --from BASE           start from this curve and change only what you give

--------------------------------------------------
VERB fan smart
usage: truesense fan smart [-h] [{on,off,toggle,status}]

positional arguments:
  {on,off,toggle,status}

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

AREA gpu
usage: truesense gpu [-h] {status,set,undervolt} ...

positional arguments:
  {status,set,undervolt}
    undervolt           GPU undervolt profiles (clock-curve offset + clock
                        cap; reset on reboot; applying needs --confirm): get |
                        list | show NAME | use NAME --confirm | reset | copy
                        NAME [NEW] | save NAME --offset MHZ [--cap MHZ] |
                        delete NAME | boot NAME|off --confirm

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

VERB gpu undervolt
usage: truesense gpu undervolt [-h] [--offset OFFSET] [--cap CAP] [--confirm]
                               [--force]
                               {get,list,show,use,reset,copy,save,delete,boot}
                               [name] [new]

positional arguments:
  {get,list,show,use,reset,copy,save,delete,boot}
  name
  new

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --offset OFFSET
  --cap CAP
  --confirm             I understand this can crash games or the driver
  --force               allow values beyond the danger line

AREA update
usage: truesense update [-h] {check,apply,auto,auto-run} ...

positional arguments:
  {check,apply,auto,auto-run}
    check               ask GitHub for the newest release
    apply               download the newest release and run its installer
                        (asks for administrator rights)
    auto                check for updates by itself once a day (a desktop
                        notification, nothing is installed)
    auto-run            ==SUPPRESS==

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

--------------------------------------------------
VERB update check
usage: truesense update check [-h] [--force]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --force     ignore the daily cache

--------------------------------------------------
VERB update apply
usage: truesense update apply [-h] [--yes] [--version VERSION]

options:
  -h, --help         show this help message and exit
  --yes              do not ask first
  --version VERSION  install this version instead of the newest, e.g. 0.3.1

--------------------------------------------------

  {on,off,toggle,status}

======================================================================
AREA keyboard
usage: truesense keyboard [-h]
                          {status,on,off,toggle,restore,list-keys,effect,fx,speed,color,paint,layout,design,image,fill,gradient,rainbow,keys,brightness,timeout,operating,profile} ...

positional arguments:
  {status,on,off,toggle,restore,list-keys,effect,fx,speed,color,paint,layout,design,image,fill,gradient,rainbow,keys,brightness,timeout,operating,profile}
    restore             back to the stock cyan per-key state
    fx                  per-key animation on chosen keys (drawn by the key
                        service, about 5 frames a second): off | pulse | wave
                        | cycle | twinkle | rainbow | scanner | comet | ripple
                        | rain | matrix | fire | plasma | aurora | lightning |
                        confetti | starlight | mood | breathing
    speed               animation speed of the running effect, 1 (slowest) ..
                        12 (fastest)
    color               change the colour of the current effect (stays in the
                        same mode)
    paint               colour some keys and keep the rest, e.g. paint
                        w=ff0000 arrows=00ff00 esc=ffffff
    layout              key names and positions (for other tools)
    design              still designs: list | apply NAME | save NAME (yours go
                        in ~/.config/truesense/designs/NAME.json)
    image               paint a picture across the keys (needs Pillow)
    keys                per-key colours, e.g. keys "wasd=ff0000" "esc=00ff00"
                        --base 101010
    brightness          0..50 (also Fn+F11/F12)
    timeout             backlight off after 30 s of no typing
    operating           colour follows the power mode
    profile             saved lighting profiles

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

======================================================================
AREA audio
usage: truesense audio [-h]
                       {output,mic,jack,voice,repair,speaker-filter,dts} ...

positional arguments:
  {output,mic,jack,voice,repair,speaker-filter,dts}
    output              speakers / headphones while the aux jack is plugged in
    jack                what the codec sees on the 3.5 mm jack; `jack
                        headphones|headset|auto` sets how the jack is used
    voice               Purified Voice (AI mic noise reduction)
    repair              no sound? restart WirePlumber so it probes the sound
                        card again, and check that an output exists
    speaker-filter      noise filter on the output (off by default: it also
                        gates music)
    dts                 Acer DTS sound through AcerUltraX

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

--------------------------------------------------
VERB audio output
usage: truesense audio output [-h] [{status,speakers,headphones,toggle,cycle}]

positional arguments:
  {status,speakers,headphones,toggle,cycle}

options:

VERB audio mic
usage: truesense audio mic [-h] [--default-only]
                           [{status,mute,unmute,toggle,volume,boost}] [value]

positional arguments:

AREA cpu
usage: truesense cpu [-h] {info,limits,undervolt} ...

positional arguments:
  {info,limits,undervolt}
    limits              CPU power limits PL1 (sustained) and PL2 (burst) in
                        watts; no argument shows them; --auto goes back to
                        automatic
    undervolt           CPU undervolt profiles (reset on reboot; applying
                        needs --confirm): get | list | show NAME | use NAME
                        --confirm | reset | copy NAME [NEW] | save NAME --core
                        MV --cache MV | delete NAME | boot NAME|off --confirm

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit

--------------------------------------------------
VERB cpu info
usage: truesense cpu info [-h]

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit

--------------------------------------------------
VERB cpu limits
usage: truesense cpu limits [-h] [--auto] [--force] [pl1] [pl2]

positional arguments:
  pl1
  pl2

options:
  -h, --help  show this help message and exit
  --auto
  --force     allow values beyond the danger line

--------------------------------------------------
VERB cpu undervolt
usage: truesense cpu undervolt [-h] [--core CORE] [--cache CACHE] [--confirm]
                               [--force] [--plane {0,2}]
                               {get,list,show,use,reset,copy,save,delete,boot,set}
                               [name] [new]

positional arguments:
  {get,list,show,use,reset,copy,save,delete,boot,set}
  name
  new

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --core CORE
  --cache CACHE
  --confirm             I understand this can freeze or reboot the laptop
  --force               allow values beyond the danger line
  --plane {0,2}         set: 0 core, 2 cache

positional arguments:
  {status,restart,logs,check,repair}
    check               every unit, the kernel module and the control socket
                        (read-only)
    repair              get the daemon, its health timer, the module and your
                        user services running again (safe to repeat; touches
                        no setting)
